evidence.evidence_text: Multilingual Knowledge Graph Completion (KGC) aims to predict missing links with multilingual knowledge graphs.

However, existing approaches suffer from two main drawbacks: (a) alignment dependency: the multilingual KGC is always realized with joint entity or relation alignment, which introduces additional alignment models and increases the complexity of the whole framework; (b) training inefficiency: the trained model will only be used for the completion of one target KG, although the data from all KGs are used simultaneously.

However, existing approaches suffer from two main drawbacks: (a) alignment dependency: the multilingual KGC is always realized with joint entity or relation alignment, which introduces additional alignment models and increases the complexity of the whole framework; (b) training inefficiency: the trained model will only be used for the completion of one target KG, although the data from all KGs are used simultaneously.
Meanwhile, a language-sensitive multi-graph attention (LSMGA) is proposed to deal with the information inconsistency among different KGs.
Experimental results show that our model achieves significant improvements on the DBP-5L and E-PKG datasets.
